title: Harmonize embedding cache and fallback routing for similarity scorer
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The similarity/rerank endpoint experiences tail latency and uneven regional error rates during traffic spikes. We currently have three partially independent mitigation layers: a global KV prefix cache, local per-region ANN fallbacks, and a coarse circuit-breaker on the API gateway. These systems race and duplicate effort, causing inconsistent client experience and under-utilized capacity.

Goal: Create a coordinated architecture that (1) unifies cache semantics across regions, (2) applies adaptive timeouts and circuit breakers informed by cache-hit and ANN-load signals, and (3) provides deterministic fallback routing so clients see predictable latency/quality trade-offs. Deliverables: design doc, implementation of cache harmonization (TTL/consistency rules + sharding), new routing policy service, and a canary rollout with observability dashboards and regression alerts.

Scope: hosts the reranking/score endpoint used by search, recommendations, and internal evals. Work includes changes in the runtime routing layer, embeddings cache service, and the scoring worker’s admission control. Not in scope: model weight changes, embedding encoder training, or consumer-side retry logic beyond recommended client doc updates.
acceptance_criteria: Unified cache behavior documented and implemented: global prefix cache + regional local caches with clear TTL hierarchy
Adaptive timeout/circuit-breaker opens based on combined signal (cache-hit fraction, ANN queue depth, regional p50/p95 latencies)
Fallback routing deterministically chooses (1) local ANN approximate pass, (2) cached full-score pass, or (3) cross-region exact rerank, with telemetry showing expected frequency
No regression in median latency for steady-state traffic (<5% change); 95th percentile tail latency reduced by at least 20% under spike scenarios in staging
Canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback triggers for error-rate and quality drift detected by downstream eval prompts
comments: 2026-02-26 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created after incident on 2026-02-22 where EU region hit high p99 and many requests fell back to US cross-region rerank. Linked incident timeline and preliminary QPS charts: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ops/similarity-incident-20260222

2026-03-01 - Ravi Patel: Spike repro in staging using traffic replay. Observed that local ANN load doubled when global cache TTL set to 1h; with TTL 5m ANN load was ~30% lower but stale-embedding rate increased. Need TTL trade-off matrix in design doc.

2026-03-03 - Design review (Folks: Mei Chen, Jonas Verma): agreed to adopt two-tier TTL: short local TTL (5m) + longer global prefix TTL (2h) and an explicit freshness score returned in headers for downstream quality monitoring. Mei to write header format spec.

2026-03-05 - Engineering sync: Decision to implement a routing policy service (lightweight stateful controller) that subscribes to cache metrics and ANN queue depth. It will emit soft-sla budgets per-region used by the API gateway. Implemented prototype that exposes policy via gRPC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-policy/pull/87
2026-03-07 - Security review requested by Ravi: routing policy will read anonymized metrics only; no PII. Security OK pending minimal ACLs for the policy service. Ticket: SEC-2106

2026-03-08 - QA note from Priya Singh: added smoke tests for TTL behavior and a regression test that simulates region outage and ensures fallback path chosen is local ANN -> cached -> cross-region (not the reverse). Tests live in infra-tests/similarity-cache-fallback.yml

2026-03-10 - Ravi Patel: Implemented circuit-breaker changes in gateway: dynamic thresholds based on short-term QPS and ANN queue depth; wired observability: p50/p95 histograms, circuit-breaker state, routing-decisions sampled at 1% and stored in logs. Canary scheduled for 2026-03-15 at 10:00 UTC.
Pending actions: finalize design doc (Confluence) with diagram of cache sharding and fallback flow; add e2e canary runbook and automated rollback criteria to runbook (oncall + engineering).
